description:
HUMAN DECISION — no build until ruled. This wave takes ZERO destructive action on the mirror; this task exists so the exposure question stops being unowned.

THE FACT (live-counted 2026-07-10): public FRIKKern/barkpark carries 609 issues (was 442 on 2026-07-09 — growing ~100/day), 100% authored by the bridge App barkpark-bridge-frikkern (0 human-authored, 0 src:github; 134 open / 475 closed). Bodies are full internal engineering prose with file:line paths (e.g. api/assets/paper-editor/src/markdown.js, tooling/tasks/tasks.mjs), internal doc_ids and acceptance checklists; labels leak worker identities (worker:fable-main, worker:cmux-smoke-...), priority and status. This is the "one board" vision working exactly as designed — the question is whether that design is the intent. Re-count at ruling time; do not trust 609 to hold.

THE OPTIONS (each with its real, explorer-verified cost):
1. KEEP AS PUBLIC ROADMAP — zero code. Deliberate transparency; exposure (file:line + worker identities) grows with every task mirrored.
2. DATASET SCOPING (already exists) — env :github_mirror_datasets (settings.ex:149-159). Coarse all-or-nothing per dataset; does NOTHING about the 609 already out.
3. LABEL/GOAL/WORKSPACE ALLOWLIST — one new cond clause in MirrorJob.reconcile (mirror_job.ex:185-220), after the intake/detached gates, before converge; new cancel reason {:cancel, :out_of_scope}. CANNOT live in Outbox (it reads mutation_events, which has no task-content columns). Hides FUTURE tasks only; the 609 stay.
4. BODY-STRIPPING — Projection.body/4 (projection.ex:220-234) replaces the description brief with minimal text. MUST preserve the "Task: <doc_id>" trailer (D11 / pr-task-gate) and the acceptance-criteria checkboxes (the flagship liveness signal). The body feeds the drift fingerprint (mirror_job.ex:426), so stripping re-fingerprints and re-PATCHes each of the 609 on its NEXT mutation; already-leaked bodies persist until then.
5. PRIVATE REPO — privatizing FRIKKern/barkpark itself COLLIDES with past-mistake #9: deploy/azure-base-install.sh:31 clones via unauthenticated HTTPS, prod deploy is a plain git pull, and the Go module path github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark needs public fetch. Effectively DEAD without a fleet-wide auth retrofit. Variant: point Settings.repo at a SEPARATE private repo (code-cheap config change) — but it breaks the one-board vision: issues no longer co-located with the code/PRs, and Task:-trailer/pr-task-gate references go cross-repo.

LOAD-BEARING FACTS FOR THE RULING:
- NO reap verb exists (Github.Client has create/get/update/close_issue/create_comment — no delete_issue; no bulk/unmirror anywhere in the plugin). NO option above removes the 609 already-minted issues without building a reaper first.
- Bulk-CLOSING them by hand is NOT clean: inbound close on a synced task is :ignored (inbound_events.ex:151-162), but each task's NEXT edit REOPENS its issue (D7 ledger-wins) and records an out_of_band_edit conflict — a slow reopen storm, one drift row per touched task.
- Bulk-DELETING them detaches only LAZILY: issues.deleted keys gh-<num> which never matches an outbound-mirrored slug, so detach fires via 410-on-next-mutation (mirror_job.ex:493-509); dormant/terminal tasks keep stale synced links forever.

TO RULE: stamp the chosen option (+ parameters, e.g. the allowlist key or the strip template) as evidence on criterion 1 of this task. The lead then files the follow-up build slice(s) under github-bridge-epic (or ratifies public-roadmap intent in the charter) and closes this task.

Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-github-bridge-epic-charter.md ("Wave 2026-07-10 — LIVE-PROOF CUT FIRED", decision 4).

purpose.why: The parent bridge is working as designed, but that design currently publishes hundreds of App-authored issues containing internal file paths, acceptance checklists, doc ids, and worker labels. Because every remedy has product and migration costs, silently changing behavior or bulk-deleting issues would be destructive and could break the one-board contract. This task forces a human policy choice, fresh counts, and parameterized follow-up before code or mirror state changes.
